thread.title: Mid-Day Update: Wall Street Rallies As US/China Trade Talks Back On

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day Update: Wall Street Rallies As US/China Trade Talks Back On
text:
Shutterstock photo Hopes for a trade agreement between the US and China coupled with upbeat quarterly results from Walmart ( WMT ) and Cisco ( CSCO ) set in motion a relief rally on Wall Street that fueled a 400+ point gain in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Bargain hunting in the beaten down energy stocks drove the entire sector higher by 1% while industrials are getting an added boost from the softer dollar.
Wall Street put aside Turkey's financial crisis and its contagion on emerging markets to focus instead on an upcoming meeting between US and Chinese trade representatives later this month. Shares of US multinationals raced higher, led by blue chips Boeing ( BA ), Caterpillar ( CAT ) and Apple ( AAPL ) with Apple setting another record high.
Data released this morning failed to dent the bull run in stocks even as the Philadelphia Fed business outlook index fell to its lowest level since Nov 2016, and July housing starts were down year-over-year for the second month in a row. The only bright spot was another drop in initial jobless claims to 212,000 for the week ended Aug. 11.
In recent earnings, Walmart lunged to its highest level since February after handily beating Wall Street's expectations and raising its full-year EPS guidance above estimates. Cisco, another Dow component stock, reported better-than-expected gains in profit and sales, lifting its stock price to within striking distance of its all-time high. Shares of JC Penney (JCP), however, tumbled to their lowest level on record as the company's Q2 loss widened more than expected and revenue fell 8% from a year ago.
Europe's stock markets were higher as positive trade developments eclipsed European banks' exposure to the Turkish currency crisis. France's CAC outperformed with a gain of 0.83%, followed by the German DAX and FTSE-100.
Crude oil was up $0.41 to $65.42 per barrel. Natural gas was down $0.03 to $2.91 per 1 million BTU. Gold was up $1.00 to $1,185.90 an ounce, while silver was up $0.27 to $14.72 an ounce. Copper was up $0.06 to $2.62 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was up 0.81% to 13.62 with the United States Natural Gas Fund up 0.75% to 23.96. Among precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was down 0.31% to 18.60 while SPDR Gold Shares were up 0.34% to 111.57. The iShares Silver Trust was up 2.03% to 13.85.
